title: Initiating a project: purpose, objectives and context
blurb: Explain why the initiation stage builds solid foundations before significant spend, what it must make clear and how it starts and ends.
question: Which process establishes solid foundations so the business understands the work before committing significant expenditure, and what triggers it?

teach.body: Formally: the purpose of initiating a project is to establish solid foundations for the project, so the business understands the work needed to deliver the project product before committing to any significant expenditure or resources. In plain English: before the big money is spent, the initiation stage works out properly why, what, how, when, at what cost and who decides.

teach.body: The full business case is what the board uses to authorize the project, and it becomes the basis for checking that the project stays viable. The project initiation documentation (PID) gathers the management products created or updated in initiation and is used to gain authorization. With the current stage plan, it forms the 'contract' between the project manager and the board.

teach.body: Brightwater Housing Association plans new heating in 400 flats. A board member wants contractors on site the week initiation is authorized. Project manager Fatima Okafor explains that initiation comes first: a full business case with costed options, a project plan, a quality approach agreed with residents' representatives and a communication approach for tenants. Only when the board approves the PID will significant contractor spend be committed.

teach.text: Classic traps: initiation IS the first stage (starting up a project is pre-project). 'Viable and worthwhile?' is the starting up question; 'solid foundations before significant spend' is initiation's. The project plan and the full business case are made in initiating a project, not in starting up. Delivery does not begin until the board authorizes the project.

items: Purpose: solid foundations so the business understands the work before significant spend.
Objectives: a common understanding of reasons, scope, delivery and cost, decision-makers, quality, baselines, risks and issues, progress, communication and policies.
Trigger: the initiation notice from authorize initiation; it is the initiation stage.
Ends with the request for project authorization; the board decides on the PID.

summary: You can now state the purpose and objectives of initiating a project and explain its context: triggered by the board's authorization, carried out in the initiation stage, and ending with a request for project authorization based on the PID and full business case.

A.q: What is the purpose of the initiating a project process?
options: To ensure the prerequisites for initiating the project are in place
To establish solid foundations before significant spend is committed
To let the board be accountable while delegating daily management
To confirm acceptance of the project product and close the project
A.why: Initiating a project establishes solid foundations so the business understands the work before committing significant expenditure or resources (15.1).

whyNot.0: Putting the prerequisites for initiation in place is the purpose of starting up a project.
whyNot.2: Board accountability with delegated daily management is the purpose of directing a project.
whyNot.3: Confirming acceptance and closing belongs to closing a project.

A.q: What triggers the initiating a project process?
options: The initiation notice from the board
The project mandate
The request for project authorization
The project product description
A.why: Initiating a project starts when the board, in authorize initiation, issues the initiation notice.

whyNot.1: The project mandate triggers starting up a project.
whyNot.2: The request for project authorization is how initiating a project ends.
whyNot.3: The PPD is created in starting up a project; it is an input, not the trigger.

A.q: In which part of the project lifecycle is initiating a project carried out?
options: Pre-project
The first delivery stage
The initiation stage
The final stage
A.why: Initiating a project is the work of the initiation stage, the first management stage of every PRINCE2 project.

whyNot.0: Pre-project is when starting up a project runs.
whyNot.1: Delivery stages follow initiation and use controlling a stage and managing product delivery.
whyNot.3: The final stage contains closing a project.

B.q:
Which two statements describe objectives of initiating a project?
1. Ensure there is authority to close the project.
2. Ensure a common understanding of how baselines will be established and controlled.
3. Ensure individuals are appointed to carry out the initiation work.
4. Ensure a common understanding of who needs information, in what format and when.
options: 1 and 2
1 and 3
2 and 4
3 and 4
B.why: Initiation aims for a common understanding of how baselines are established and controlled (2) and of who needs information, in what format and when (4) (15.2).

whyNot.0: Statement 1 is an objective of directing a project.
whyNot.1: Statement 1 belongs to directing a project and statement 3 to starting up a project.
whyNot.3: Statement 3 is an objective of starting up a project, which appoints people before initiation.

B.q: Which product does the board use to authorize the project and then as the basis for checking that the project remains viable?
options: The outline business case
The project brief
The benefits management approach
The full business case
B.why: The full business case, prepared in initiation, is used by the board to authorize the project and is the basis for the ongoing check of viability.

whyNot.0: The outline business case supports the decision to initiate and is developed into the full business case.
whyNot.1: The project brief supports authorize initiation and is superseded by the PID.
whyNot.2: The benefits management approach is reviewed when authorizing the project, but viability is judged from the business case.

B.q: Why does PRINCE2 require an initiation stage before delivery begins?
options: So the business understands the work before committing major spend
So the board can test whether the idea is worth initiating
So team managers can start building the first products early
So the business layer can appoint the executive and PM
B.why: Initiation lets the business understand the work needed before committing significant expenditure or resources (15.1).

whyNot.1: Testing whether an idea is worth initiating is the job of starting up a project.
whyNot.2: Specialist products are built in delivery stages, after the project is authorized.
whyNot.3: The executive and PM are appointed in starting up a project.

C.q: Which process produces the full business case, and which board activity uses it to decide whether to proceed?
options: Initiating a project; authorize the project
Starting up a project; authorize initiation
Initiating a project; authorize initiation
Managing a stage boundary; authorize the project
C.why: The full business case is prepared in initiating a project, and the board relies on it in authorize the project to decide whether to proceed.

whyNot.1: Starting up a project produces the outline business case, which supports authorize initiation.
whyNot.2: The process is right, but authorize initiation happens before the full business case exists.
whyNot.3: Managing a stage boundary updates the business case later; it does not create the full version.

C.q: A board member wants the supplier to start building as soon as initiation is authorized, before any PID exists. Which statement best explains why PRINCE2 does not support this?
options: Delivery waits until the business layer approves each product
Delivery waits until the lessons log has been closed
Delivery waits until every stage plan has been approved
Delivery waits until the board authorizes the project on the PID
C.why: Delivery stages begin only after the board, in authorize the project, approves the PID and full business case; starting delivery before then skips a decision point.

whyNot.0: The business layer does not approve individual products.
whyNot.1: The lessons log stays open throughout the project and is reviewed at closure.
whyNot.2: Stage plans are approved one at a time near the end of the previous stage, not all at once.

C.q: Which objective of initiating a project is supported by agreeing the communication management approach?
options: Common understanding of how quality will be achieved
Common understanding of who needs information and when
Common understanding of the reasons and benefits
Common understanding of how risks will be controlled
C.why: The communication management approach sets out the means and frequency of communication, supporting a common understanding of who needs information, in what format and when.

whyNot.0: How quality will be achieved is set out in the quality management approach.
whyNot.2: Reasons and benefits are documented in the full business case.
whyNot.3: How risks are controlled is set out in the risk management approach.

reteach.title: Survey before you build
reteach.question: Why not just start building once the board has agreed to look at the idea?

blocks.body: Starting up a project said the idea is worth a closer look. Initiating a project is that closer look: a costed plan, a full business case and agreed ways of handling quality, risk, issues, change and communication. Only then is the board asked to commit to the whole project. Spending on delivery before this risks money on work nobody has properly understood.

blocks.text: Two questions, two processes: 'worth initiating?' is starting up; 'do we understand it well enough to commit?' is initiating.

explain.body: Establish solid foundations so the business understands the work needed to deliver the project product before committing to significant expenditure or resources.

test.q: Which question best captures the purpose of initiating a project?
options: Is the work understood before major spend?
Do we have a viable and worthwhile project?
Is the current stage within its tolerances?
Has the project product been accepted?
test.why: Initiating a project makes sure the work is understood before significant expenditure or resources are committed (15.1).

whyNot.1: 'Viable and worthwhile?' is the question for starting up a project.
whyNot.2: Stage tolerances are monitored in controlling a stage.
whyNot.3: Acceptance of the project product is confirmed in closing a project.

explain.body: A common understanding of: the reasons, benefits and risks; scope and products; how, when and at what cost; who decides; how quality is achieved; how baselines are controlled; how risks and issues are handled; how progress is controlled; who needs information; and how business policies apply.

test.q: Which is an objective of initiating a project?
options: Authority to close the project when it is complete
Appointing the executive and the project manager
Agreeing work packages with each team manager
Common understanding of how progress is monitored
test.why: A common understanding of how progress will be monitored and controlled is one of the initiation objectives (15.2).

whyNot.0: Authority to close is an objective of directing a project.
whyNot.1: Appointing the executive and PM happens in starting up a project.
whyNot.2: Work packages are agreed in controlling a stage and managing product delivery.

explain.body: Triggered by the initiation notice from authorize initiation, using the project brief and initiation stage plan. It is the initiation stage and ends with a request for project authorization; managing a stage boundary plans the first delivery stage as initiation ends.

test.q: How does the initiating a project process end?
options: With a request for project initiation
With a closure notification to the business
With a request for project authorization
With an initiation notice to the team
test.why: Initiating a project ends with the project manager requesting project authorization from the board (15.4.7).

whyNot.0: The request for project initiation ends starting up a project.
whyNot.1: A closure notification is sent by the board when it authorizes project closure.
whyNot.3: The initiation notice comes from the board at the start of initiation, not the end.

explain.body: The PID brings together the management products created or updated in initiation. The version used to gain authorization is baselined and placed under change control. It is reviewed and updated at stage boundaries, and the end project report compares results with it.

test.q: What happens to the version of the PID used to gain authorization?
options: It is replaced by the project brief at once
It is baselined and placed under change control
It is archived until the project closes
It is sent to team managers as work packages
test.why: The version of the PID used to gain authorization is baselined and placed under change control (15.4.6).

whyNot.0: It is the other way round: the PID supersedes the project brief.
whyNot.2: The PID stays in use: it is reviewed and updated at each stage boundary.
whyNot.3: Work packages are separate products authorized in controlling a stage.
